essence: Light-formed Śiva-tattva cannot enter the undivided mandala — seeing autonomy, it falls into non-conceptual Bhairava-immersion; teaching: all states are reflection in knowing's sky.
Taste loses primacy: its works run through an occult eye.
Smell and touch lose primacy too: qualitied, they fail where the qualitied is absent — the effect-chain never starts from them.
Yet they are not nonexistent — body-stripping and seed attest their presence.
Sound loses primacy: a speaker is required, and it reaches us like an echo.
The world shines as reflection in the Supreme Lord's light, no self-luminosity below him.
The questioner's image is dissolved: let there be nothing at all standing there.
The apparent causelessness resolves into svātantrya-śakti — the Lord's power, synonym of autonomy, bears the world's reflection and so owns world-selfhood.
Self-nature contemplation would be inertness — saved from that only by being inseparable from consciousness-nature, the womb of supreme sound.
Three primary powers encode the bīja-triads: a i u for unsurpassable will-awakening, ā ī ū for action-power's onset.
Prior triad sun-natured by light-essence, final triad moon-natured by rest-bliss — the boundary where action-portion stops entering.
Action entering will and rulership births iṣyamāṇa/īśyamāṇa: ra by mere light, la by rest — heard, not expressed.
The r-quad is neuter because it carries both shades.
Surpassable-bliss spread in will yields the pair e oṃ.
The union of surpassable bliss adds ai au.
Action-power itself is the quad e ai o au.
At action-power's end all stands as effect — the prior standing as point, am, until unsurpassable entry.
From that point the unsurpassable's own visarga is born: aḥ.
The contemplation-seeds total sixteen — parāmarśa's bīja-form declared.
From those seeds rises the expression-natured womb-form.
Consonant-classes distribute over the powers: ka of faith, ca of object-will, double ṭa/ta of awakening, pa of fivefold union.
Letter-clusters carry generation-grounds — unmeṣa-lineage for ya-ra-lā, visarga-lineage for śa-ṣa-sā, yoni-born kṣa.
The whole scheme terminates in theology: anuttara as kuleśvara.
One kaulic visarga-throb externalizes the class-contemplations into tattva-forms.
The visarga is threefold as mind's rest, awakening, and dissolution — āṇava, śākta, śāṃbhava.
World-birth is visarga-operation itself — no separate creator-will needed.
Undivided contemplation collapses Lord and power into the one seed-womb; divided, the power-endowed/power dyad stands.
Eightfold yields nine classes with the wheel-Lord; each-contemplation-prevalence yields fifty.
Possible part-difference raises the count to eighty.
Reality holds six contemplations, twelve by spreading-and-returning — feeding the Lord's world-power fullness.
These contemplating powers are the Lord's — named Śrīkālikā.
Pure contemplations stand in pure knowledge as para-apara, contracting māyā's awakening into knower/known natures.
Māyic divisions revive under pure contemplations into vigors granting both enjoyment and liberation — the view ends in liberated-while-living.
Even here, as before, mantra and the like impose no obstruction.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vimarśa weight (rest carrying the letter-scheme)
rasa.sthayibhava: viśrānti (rest as the ground the bījas stand in)
rasa.justification: The relish is ordered disclosure: each refutation settles, each seed names, each count lands — and the chapter's own doctrine says rest is bliss, so its calm is content, not mood; the jīvanmuktatā close is the single rising chord.

sections.FUNCTION: Maps the parāmarśa-śakti doctrine: why the reflected world is not primary, the sixteen bīja-seeds of contemplation, the consonant-classes distributed over the powers, the threefold visarga, and the counts (9/50/80/6/12) that nourish the Lord's world-power — closing with Śrīkālikā, māyic revival, and jīvanmuktatā.
sections.KEY TERMS: pratibimba (reflection in bodha-gagana); svātantrya-śakti (autonomy-power as the real hetu); parāmarśa (contemplation as the bīja-substance); ṣoḍaśaka-bīja (the sixteen seeds a…aḥ); varga-distribution (consonant-classes over śaktis); visarga-tridhā (āṇava/śākta/śāṃbhava); Śrīkālikā (the contemplating powers' name); jīvanmuktatā (the śāṃbhava-samāveśa close).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Āhnika 3 follows the pratibimba opening of the ahnika-series and turns cosmology into phonology; the ra/la and bīja scheme feeds nothing later in Tantrasāra — a self-contained doctrine of letter-and-power; a14's rite-manual is the practical opposite face of this theory.
sections.BOUNDARY: Reflection doctrine argued by simile-chain, not by exclusion of other models; the counts (16/9/50/80/6/12) asserted without derivation shown; māyic revival stated as fact with no conditions given; mantra-freedom (u34) declared by appeal to 'as before' without restating the prior ground.
sections.EXPLANATION: The chapter moves: refutation of primaries (rasa/gandha/sparśa/śabda all derivative) → the reflection-model scaled to viśva → svātantrya-śakti as the real reason → the bīja-scheme (a i u … aḥ = sixteen) → consonant-classes mapped to powers → visarga as world-birth engine → combinatorial counts → Śrīkālikā → pure/māyic parāmarśas → revivification and the jīvanmuktatā close. Sound is doctrine here: every letter names a power-state.
sections.RELATED: GRETIL Tantrasāra ahnika 3 (KSTS 17); Tantrāloka cosmology parallels (lore); a12/a14 samāveśa and rite faces; qa NEEDS_WITNESS expected.
